abstract.text: Canonical diagrams of Boolean functions and families of sets.
A shared table of zero-suppressed decision diagrams: families of sets drawn from the elements
, each a directed acyclic graph whose vertices test one element and branch
to a low child (the sets without it) and a high child (the sets with it, the element removed),
down to the constants: the empty family and the family holding only the empty set (Minato,
“Zero-Suppressed BDDs for Set Manipulation in Combinatorial Problems”, 1993).
The table’s vertices as a directed acyclic graph: a vertex per diagram vertex, 0 the empty
family and 1 the family {∅}, and from each other vertex a low edge and a high edge, which
tells apart. A family’s diagram is the part reachable from its
Every low and high edge, by source.
